steps.name: Sample structure QC and low-depth sample assessment
steps.question: Do the 12 skin samples (6 AD lesional vs 6 control) cluster by condition, and how does the flagged low-depth sample (sample_01, ~4x below median library size) behave on PCA and sample-distance metrics relative to its group?

grounding.reason: R-0033 mandates blind-VST/PCA/sample-distance QC before modeling; R-0008 requires keeping and reporting the low-depth sample rather than silently dropping it.

acceptance_criteria: Blind VST is applied to raw counts and PCA + Euclidean sample-distance heatmap are produced, colored by condition
Library size and detected-gene count for every sample, with sample_01 explicitly annotated as ~4x below median
A stated, evidence-based decision on whether sample_01 is retained or excluded from downstream DE (default: retained per DESeq2 size-factor handling unless it is also an outlier on PCA/clustering)

steps.name: Filter low-count genes and build DESeq2 dataset
steps.question: Which of the 12000 genes in counts.csv have sufficient read support (>=10 counts in >=6 samples, the smallest group size) to be tested for differential expression between lesional and control skin?

grounding.reason: Minimal pre-filter of >=10 counts in >=smallest-group-size samples per rule R-0002/R-0029; DESeq2 handles normalization internally so no external scaling is applied.

acceptance_criteria: Genes retained require >=10 counts in at least 6 samples (min group size)
Filter is stated as minimal pre-filter only; independent filtering at the results step is not bypassed
Number of genes entering the model vs. excluded by the pre-filter is reported

steps.name: DESeq2 Wald test: AD lesional vs control
steps.question: Which genes are significantly differentially expressed between AD lesional and control skin (design ~condition, reference level = control, contrast condition lesional_vs_control), with size-factor normalization accounting for sample_01's depth?

grounding.reason: Standard DESeq2 Wald + apeglm shrinkage path for a 6v6 unpaired design with an explicit reference level, BH/independent filtering at alpha 0.05, and required fit diagnostics.

acceptance_criteria: Design formula ~condition with condition releveled so 'control' is the explicit reference
DESeq() run with median-of-ratios size factors (no external normalization applied)
Wald test results extracted via a named contrast (condition, lesional, control)
apeglm LFC shrinkage applied to the lesional_vs_control coefficient; both shrunken and unshrunken log2FC plus lfcSE reported per gene
BH-adjusted p-values with independent filtering at alpha=0.05; genes selected by padj<0.05 only
MA plot and dispersion plot produced as fit diagnostics; p-value histogram inspected before adjustment
Genes with NA padj from Cook's-distance outlier flagging reported separately from those removed by independent filtering

steps.name: edgeR quasi-likelihood cross-check and consensus DE set
steps.question: Do the genes called significant by DESeq2 (padj<0.05) agree with an independent edgeR quasi-likelihood F-test fit on the same filtered counts and design, and what is the high-confidence intersection set?

grounding.reason: At 6 replicates/group, running both DESeq2 Wald and edgeR QLF and reporting the intersection as the high-confidence set is the recommended robustness check.

acceptance_criteria: edgeR QLF fit uses TMM normalization and the same design (~condition, control as reference) on the same filtered gene set
Number of significant genes (FDR<0.05) reported for each method separately
Intersection (high-confidence set) and method-specific-only gene lists reported explicitly; union is not presented as 'the result'

steps.name: GSVA hallmark pathway scores + limma group test
steps.question: Which of the 50 MSigDB Hallmark pathways show a shifted per-sample activity score between AD lesional and control skin?

grounding.reason: Knowledge-check rejected fgsea-preranked-on-Hallmark as the enrichment method for this exact situation (R-0048 flagged it as not permitted here); GSVA per-sample scores + limma is the method the check accepted (ok:true) and gives a per-sample pathway score matrix as the question implies ('which hallmark pathways change').

acceptance_criteria: GSVA computed per sample on normalized (e.g., vst or log-CPM) expression using the MSigDB human Hallmark gene sets (50 sets), Poisson or Gaussian kernel stated explicitly
Sample_01 included in the score matrix with its score visible alongside other samples (not silently excluded)
limma moderated t-test run on the GSVA score matrix with the same ~condition design and reference level as the DE model
BH-adjusted p-values reported per hallmark pathway; pathways at adjusted p<0.05 flagged as changed
Gene set collection name and version (MSigDB Hallmark human 2026.1) stated in the output

steps.name: GO and Reactome/WikiPathways over-representation on significant DE genes
steps.question: Which Gene Ontology biological processes and Reactome/WikiPathways pathways are over-represented among the genes significantly changed (padj<0.05) between AD lesional and control skin, using the tested genes as background?

grounding.reason: R-0103 flags that ORA on a short significant-gene list has low power; step is included as a secondary, explicitly-caveated read-out alongside the primary GSVA+limma pathway-level test, and reports the size of the significant list per the rule.

acceptance_criteria: Universe restricted to genes that passed the pre-filter and were tested by DESeq2 (not whole genome)
GO BP over-representation run with clusterProfiler::enrichGO against org.Hs.eg.db, followed by rrvgo semantic-similarity term reduction to representative terms
Reactome and WikiPathways over-representation run separately against the same universe using the local Reactome/WikiPathways human gene sets, with each release/version reported
If fewer than ~50 genes pass padj<0.05, the report states this explicitly and treats the ORA result as low-powered per the size-of-list caveat
Gene symbols mapped to Entrez IDs via org.Hs.eg.db for the GO/Reactome step; unmapped gene share reported

steps.name: Integrated DE + hallmark pathway report
steps.question: What is the consolidated, reproducible summary of differentially expressed genes and hallmark/GO/Reactome pathway changes between AD lesional and control skin, including how the low-depth sample was handled?

grounding.reason: Consolidated reporting requirements per rules covering DE reporting completeness, enrichment reporting completeness, fit diagnostics, and reproducibility record.

acceptance_criteria: Report states: package versions, design formula, reference level, contrast, thresholds (padj<0.05), pre-filter, number of genes tested, number of DE genes (DESeq2 vs edgeR vs intersection)
Report includes MA plot, dispersion plot, p-value histogram, and volcano plot (shrunken log2FC vs -log10 padj)
Report states the sample_01 depth issue and the QC-based decision on its inclusion/exclusion with justification
GSVA hallmark result table (pathway, limma t, p, padj) and GO/Reactome ORA tables included with gene-set collection versions and universe stated
Reproducibility record included: sessionInfo, random seeds, gene-set collection versions (Hallmark 2026.1, Reactome current, GO 2026.1)
Enrichment method-dependence caveat stated explicitly (GSVA/limma result is not treated as sole ground truth; ORA is secondary and caveated for list size)

plan.title: AD lesional vs control DE + hallmark pathways
plan.analytical_narrative: 12 skin samples (6 AD lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch, raw Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes) are analyzed with the standard DESeq2 count-based DE workflow. Sample_01's library size (~4x below median) is inspected but not silently dropped: it goes through sample-structure QC (blind VST, PCA, sample-distance heatmap) and DESeq2's own size-factor normalization, which is the correct way to account for depth differences without discarding information; a decision to exclude it is only made if it also fails on PCA/clustering, and that decision is stated explicitly with a reason. DE is tested with the DESeq2 Wald test with apeglm LFC shrinkage, cross-checked with an edgeR quasi-likelihood fit to report a high-confidence intersection set (rule R-0001/R-0042). Genes are called by BH-adjusted p<0.05 with independent filtering (never by raw p or fold-change alone). Because the knowledge-service check rejects fgsea-on-Hallmark for this exact situation and instead permits GSVA-per-sample-scores+limma as the pathway-level method here, pathway change is assessed with GSVA hallmark pathway scores per sample followed by a limma test of those scores between conditions — giving both a per-sample pathway score matrix and a group-level significance test. GO over-representation (enrichGO + rrvgo) and a Reactome/WikiPathways-based over-representation pass on the significant gene list are added as secondary, complementary functional read-outs, each restricted to the tested-gene universe per rule R-0046/R-0054. All thresholds, package versions, and the reproducibility record (sessionInfo, seeds, collection versions) are captured in the final report.

keep gene with >=10 counts in >=6 samples (smallest group size)
design ~ condition, explicit reference level = control, named contrast condition_lesional_vs_control
fgsea preranked GSEA on Wald stat, MSigDB Hallmark then Reactome
DE + enrichment report with diagnostics, reproducibility record

GSVA per-sample pathway scores (MSigDB Hallmark gene sets) followed by limma differential test on the scores between lesional and control
